chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hammani, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both):

Hisham ibn al-Hakam claimed that Allah is a body, there is nothing whatsoever like unto Him, the All-knowing, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Omnipotent, the Speaker, and the Communicator. Speech, Omnipotence, and Knowledge flow from the One Same Source, none of these things are created. So he (AS) said: May Allah kill him! Does he not know that a body is limited, and that speech is other than the speaker? Allah forbid, I am free from such words. He is devoid of both body and image. He has no limits, and everything other than Him is created. Verily, everything that exists is the result of His Will and Intent which is expressed without words, the use of the tongue, or any reluctance or hesitation.

key_terms.ليس كمثله شيء: There is nothing whatsoever like unto Him

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on whether Allah has a physical body or form?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) refutes Hisham ibn al-Hakam’s Mu'tazili-leaning view that divine attributes like speech and knowledge are created entities by asserting that Allah is devoid of body, form, and limitation. He clarifies that while all things are created by His Will, His attributes are not separate created things but are expressed through His command without physical organs or hesitation, a key distinction in Shia theological discourse on Tawhid.
